name: eu.paymentslaw/legislation
title: EU Payments Law
description: Read, compare and cite EU payments legislation (PSD2, RTS-SCA, PSD3, PSR, DORA), source attached.

tools.name: get_provision
tools.description: Use this to read or quote an EU legislative provision, such as PSD2 Article 97 or RTS-SCA Article 5. Returns the source text of an article, annex or recital as markdown, with its cite anchor, provenance and text state; a long provision paginates by structural block. version_id is optional, and a pinned version id is refused with the URL where that text is published. include_correspondences adds the cross-instrument article equivalences. cites and terms_used list what the returned text cites in other acts and the defined terms it uses, with the call that opens each.

instrument_id.description: Registry id of the instrument, e.g. "psd-2".

version_id.description: Omit, or pass "current", for the served text. A pinned version id returns version_not_served with the URL where that text is published.

kind.description: Which kind of provision the locator names.

paragraph.description: Numbered paragraph within the article, e.g. "2".

point.description: Lettered point within the paragraph, e.g. "b".

annex.description: Annex number, roman or arabic ("I", "1"); omit for an instrument whose single annex is unnumbered.

on_date.description: ISO date; returns the provision-level applicability view.

cursor.description: Continue a paginated provision. Bound to the release.

include_correspondences.description: Off by default. When true, an article carries correspondences[]: the cross-instrument article equivalences the corpus publishes, each with the counterpart's own get_provision locator, version and cite anchor. null means the release predates the mapping table, not that the article has none.

tools.name: get_instrument
tools.description: Use this to check an EU instrument's recorded legal status, source version, dates and amendments, including whether a held PSR or PSD3 text is a proposal, a Council compromise text, a Council position at first reading or the act published in the Official Journal. Metadata, dates, lifecycle and application events, and curated relationships, each naming the operative amending or repealing article where curated. No article index: use list_provisions. Pass on_date for the applicability record on that date.

on_date.description: ISO date; returns the full applicability record.

tools.name: list_instruments
tools.description: Use this to discover which EU instruments are held before a coverage question, or find their registry ids and legal status. Paginated, filterable by status, category, core/supplementary, and by whether an instrument was in force on a given date. For corpus-coverage questions, filter by category here, enumerate each instrument with list_provisions, then open what you need with get_provision.

status.description: Legal status at the release, e.g. "in_force".

in_force_on_date.description: ISO date; keeps instruments in force on that date.

tools.name: get_source_notes
tools.description: Use this to read the original legislative footnotes and source-note bodies for a held instrument, including preamble and annex notes. Omit note_key for the paginated inventory; supply an exact returned key to retrieve one. Keys retain source scope because printed markers may repeat. This tool does not infer ownership by a provision. Historical versions return an explicit version_not_served link.

version_id.description: Omit or use current for the served version; pinned versions return an explicit version_not_served link.

note_key.description: Exact key returned by this tool. Omit to list notes. Printed markers may be reused and are not necessarily unique keys.

limit.description: Notes per page, default 10; complete bodies are never truncated.

cursor.description: Continue with the same arguments; bound to this corpus release.

tools.name: list_provisions
tools.description: Use this to browse an EU instrument's article, annex or recital index, or list its provisions tagged with a topic, a starting point for a coverage question. Metadata only: each item carries the exact locator get_provision accepts. Articles and annexes by default; pass kind=recital for recitals.

chapter.description: Keep only provisions under a division whose heading contains this text, e.g. "operational risk". Any heading above the provision counts (Part, Title, Chapter or Section); case is ignored.

topic.description: Keep only provisions carrying this topic tag. Tags are rule-derived and can miss a provision, so a filtered list is not everything on the subject.

tools.name: search_legislation
tools.description: Use this to find EU legislative provisions on payment-services questions: strong customer authentication (SCA), dynamic linking, open banking, safeguarding and payment liability. For exact wording use get_provision; for defined-term wording use get_defined_term. Full-text search across articles, annexes and recitals, ranked in that order; a citation-shaped query resolves through the citation grammar first. Every hit carries the locator get_provision accepts, its cite anchor and the matched passage. topic narrows hits rather than widening them, so for a coverage question ('everything on X') pick the instruments with list_instruments, enumerate each with list_provisions filtered by topic, search each for the terms as well, then open them with get_provision.

query.description: EU legislative search terms, e.g. "strong customer authentication", "dynamic linking", "safeguarding" or "DORA ICT risk". Use words expected in the legal text, not an entire advice request. Quoted phrases are honoured; AND, OR and NOT are the only operators. A citation-shaped query ("Article 97(1) PSD2") is resolved through the citation grammar first.

kind.description: Restrict to one source type. Articles, annexes and recitals are all searched by default, ranked in that order of authority.

topic.description: Keep only provisions carrying this topic tag. Tags are rule-derived and can miss a provision, so a filtered list is not everything on the subject.

in_force_on_date.description: ISO date; keeps hits from instruments in force on that date, on the same semantics list_instruments uses.

tools.name: resolve_citation
tools.description: Use this to resolve a written EU legal citation, such as Article 97(1) PSD2, into an instrument and provision locator. For a topic rather than a citation, use search_legislation. Ranked candidates with ambiguity flagged and confidence stated: exact (instrument certain, provision found), strong (instrument certain, provision not verified or not named) or ambiguous (more than one reading). A citation of an instrument this corpus does not hold is named, with its CELEX and ELI, rather than guessed at.

citation.description: A citation in any form a reader would write: "Article 97(1) PSD2", "Art. 5a of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014", a CELEX number, an ELI path, or a bare acronym.

tools.name: search_defined_terms
tools.description: Use this to find which EU instruments define a legal term, such as payment transaction or payment account, and where their definitions differ. For definition wording use get_defined_term. A listing: term, definers and divergence flags, with no definition text. Matching is over the term itself, never the definition body. Divergence is judged on the resolved text as well as the verbatim text. Pass only_divergent to find where the corpus does not agree with itself.

query.description: Term text to match. Matching is over the TERM only, never the definition body. Omit for the full alphabetical listing of every term the corpus defines.

only_divergent.description: Keep only terms whose definers disagree — on the resolved text, the verbatim text, or both.

instrument.description: Keep only terms defined in this instrument, e.g. "psd-2".

tools.name: get_defined_term
tools.description: Use this to read and compare the held legislative definitions of a term, such as payment transaction in PSD2 and PSR. These are source definitions, not a general dictionary or a legal opinion. Every definition verbatim and resolved, clustered by what the text actually says, with the chronological and concurrent views and word-level comparisons between them. Resolution follows the cited version, never legislative succession: a definition citing a repealed act resolves to that act and is labelled repealed, not silently replaced by its successor's wording. A term the corpus does not define is refused with suggestions — nothing is substituted. references_in gives the reverse edges: which definitions lean on this one.

term.description: The defined term, as written in the legislation ("payment account"). Matched exactly after normalisation; a term the corpus does not define is refused with suggestions, never answered with a neighbouring one.

instrument.description: Narrow the definitions listed to one definer. The clusters, views and comparisons stay corpus-wide: what the term means elsewhere does not change because you asked about one instrument.

view.description: Which text clusters and comparisons run on. "resolved" (default) follows each definition's pointers to its root; "verbatim" uses the text as each instrument prints it.

on_date.description: ISO date. Adds operative_on_date and temporal_state_on_date per definer, and makes the concurrent view that date's rather than the release's.

comparison.description: Which comparisons to compute. "adjacent" (default) compares consecutive distinct clusters in chronological order; {baseline: cluster_id} compares one cluster against every other; {pair: [cite, cite]} compares two named definitions; {concurrent_pairs: {}} compares every pair that was in force at once.

tools.name: compare_versions
tools.description: Compare an article between versions of PSR or PSD3: the 2023 Commission proposal and the April 2026 Council compromise, the April compromise and the October 2026 Council position at first reading, or the 2023 proposal and the October position. Returns the word-level comparison, identifying each version, its article number and source. Either comparison direction is supported. Where numbering changed, use the article number belonging to each version; a mismatched pairing is refused with the corresponding mapping. Comparisons with Official Journal texts are not currently available. Unsupported requests return the available pairs and links to pinned texts where available. The `changes` field summarises the types of textual change.

instrument_id.description: Registry id of the instrument, e.g. "psr".

from_version_id.description: Version id one side of the pair.

from_locator.description: The article on the from side.

kind.description: Which kind of provision the locator names.

paragraph.description: Numbered paragraph within the article, e.g. "2".

point.description: Lettered point within the paragraph, e.g. "b".

annex.description: Annex number, roman or arabic ("I", "1"); omit for an instrument whose single annex is unnumbered.

to_locator.description: The article on the to side.

kind.description: Which kind of provision the locator names.

paragraph.description: Numbered paragraph within the article, e.g. "2".

point.description: Lettered point within the paragraph, e.g. "b".

annex.description: Annex number, roman or arabic ("I", "1"); omit for an instrument whose single annex is unnumbered.

tools.name: list_version_changes
tools.description: Browse article-level changes between versions of PSR or PSD3. Without version IDs, returns the latest available comparison: the April 2026 Council compromise and the October 2026 Council position at first reading. Lists aligned articles with mechanical change classifications, both article numbers where numbering changed, and any editor's notes. Filter by status, editor's note or article range; editor's notes remain included regardless of filters. For an article's word-level comparison, use `compare_versions`. Comparisons with Official Journal texts are not currently available.

from_version_id.description: Optional starting version. Supply both version IDs or neither; without them, returns the instrument's latest available comparison. Accepts a version ID or a supported alias.

to_version_id.description: Optional ending version. Supply with from_version_id; accepts the same version IDs and aliases.

status.description: One of the textual change classes, e.g. "amended_substantial" (wording changed substantially).

material_only.description: Keep only articles that carry an editor's note.

tools.name: show_changes
tools.description: Shows the reader what changed: presents a comparison or a change inventory to the reader as an interactive card, this service's intended way of showing what changed between the two texts of a served pair. With article, the card is that article's word-level comparison, side by side with every change marked, as compare_versions serves it. With articles, one card holds those articles as a filtered inventory, each opening its comparison in place. Without either, the card is the instrument's inventory of changed articles grouped by kind of change, with the editors' notes, as list_version_changes serves it. The result is a one-line summary with the site link; the card loads its own data. compare_versions and list_version_changes return the same comparison as data, for an answer that quotes or reasons over the wording.

instrument_id.description: Registry id of the instrument, e.g. "psr".

article.description: An article number. With it, the card is that article's comparison; without it and without articles, the instrument's change inventory.

articles.description: Several article numbers: one card holding those articles as a filtered inventory, each opening its comparison in place. Not with article.

from_version_id.description: Optional starting version. Supply both version IDs or neither; without them, returns the instrument's latest available comparison. Accepts a version ID or a supported alias.

to_version_id.description: Optional ending version. Supply with `from_version_id`; accepts the same version IDs and aliases.

tools.name: get_access_status
tools.description: Use this when a call was refused for want of sign-in or a licence, or when asked what this connection can use, what a licence adds or where prices are. Returns whether this connection is on the free service or a licence, what a licence adds, the address for licences and prices, and what the corpus does not hold. Takes no arguments.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Use this to find EU payments legislation on topics such as SCA, open banking and safeguarding in the held PSD2, RTS-SCA, PSD3/PSR and related instruments. Simple search returning the top hits as {id, title, url}, where id is the cite anchor fetch accepts. For filters, snippets, scores and paging use search_legislation, which returns more.

query.description: EU payments legislative terms or citation, e.g. "strong customer authentication", "safeguarding" or "Article 97 PSD2".

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Use this to open and cite an EU legislative provision found by search. Simple retrieval of one provision's text by its cite anchor id (e.g. "psd-2 Art 97"), with citation metadata. A provision longer than the response ceiling arrives in part, with metadata.complete false and a metadata.next_cursor that get_provision continues. Accepts only ids this service minted — free-text citations belong to resolve_citation. get_provision returns more: paging, applicability and typed warnings.

id.description: An id from search, or a cite anchor such as "psd-2 Art 97" or "psd-2 Recital 12", or an instrument id such as "psd-2". An optional version qualifier, e.g. "psr (com-2023-367) Art 105", retains its edition and refuses unserved text.

tools.name: get_orientation
tools.description: Use this for questions on the AI Act for payments and credit models; DORA for ICT and operational risk; SCA from PSD2 to the PSR and PSD3; and SCA for 3-D Secure practitioners, broad or specific, or when asked for a pathway or reading order. For other subjects use search_legislation. Curated reading pathways into the corpus for a stated audience: ordered waypoints with cite anchors every other tool can open, related defined terms and known pitfalls. A waypoint's or pitfall's quotes are the cited provision's own words that the line rests on. The prose is editorial and labelled as such — it maps the reading order, never legal weight. Omit the pathway argument for the catalogue; an unknown id is refused with the catalogue, nothing substituted. Catalogue entries and pathway waypoints paginate whole: follow pagination.next_cursor with the same pathway and limit until complete.

pathway.description: Pathway id from the catalogue. Omit for the catalogue.

limit.description: Maximum catalogue entries or pathway waypoints per page; whole-item byte bounds may return fewer. For a pathway, a limit of at least its waypoint count (the catalogue's `waypoints`) returns the whole pathway in one response.

cursor.description: pagination.next_cursor from this tool; repeat the same pathway and limit.
